question: To win support for a new Claude-assisted proposal-drafting arrangement, a team demonstrates the best output from about twenty attempts and does not mention the other nineteen. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The demonstration may run longer than the slot the sponsors set aside in the meeting agenda.
B) The twenty attempts consumed usage that the team had allocated to its ordinary client work.
C) The team will have to repeat the demonstration for other departments that were not present.
D) Sponsors will fund the arrangement expecting a standard the everyday output does not reach.
correct_answers: D) Sponsors will fund the arrangement expecting a standard the everyday output does not reach.
explanations: Overrunning the agenda is an inconvenience for the meeting chair. It is unrelated to the honesty of what the demonstration implies about everyday performance.
Usage spent preparing a demonstration is a minor and one-off cost. It affects the team's own budget rather than the decision the sponsors are about to make.
Repeating a demonstration costs a little time and is entirely normal when several departments are interested. It has no bearing on whether the expectations being set are accurate.

Correct. Showing the best of twenty sets the expected quality at a level the arrangement reaches roughly one time in twenty. Funding, staffing and review effort are then planned against a standard that will not materialise, and the credibility loss lands on the team.
